frozen_candidate_root_contribution: xzn contributes the holding of something in secured custody within a bounded, access-controlled enclosure, realized in two morphological faces: the patient/place face khaza'in (the reserve-repository held under exclusive or delegated ownership, from which content is released only in a controlled measure and which may be withheld) and the agent face khazin/khazana (the one who keeps such a bounded holding and governs its boundary). The distinctive core (secured reserve + metered/controlled release) is broad and adversarially clean across the store-class and its provision-keeper agent, but attenuates to bare custody-of-a-gated-enclosure in the khazana sub-class.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across 13 nominal occurrences the root splits by morphology into three faces of one custodial notion. The dominant broken plural khaza'in (8x) names God's (or, once, Egypt's) secured reserve-stores: what one owns and releases only 'in a known measure' (15:21) or could withhold rather than spend (17:100). The active participle khazinin (15:22) is the transparent agent of that same idea (humans are not the keepers/storers of the sky-water), welding the store to its keeper in one pericope (15:21-22). The agent-plural khazana (4x) are the angelic gate-custodians of Hell and the Garden, who open gates, interrogate, or welcome at the threshold but store and dispense nothing. The narrow, distinctive reserve/metered-release sense governs the first two faces (9/13); the khazana face requires retreating to the thinner, less distinctive 'custody of a gated enclosure', so it is carried as a coherent resistant sub-class rather than a live instance of the reserve-sense.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: xzn does NOT entail: (1) the act/quality of guarding or preserving (that is hfz, named separately alongside khaza'in in 12:55: Yusuf is hafiz over the khaza'in); (2) ownership/title as such (ownership rides on 'ind/li-llah/tamlikun; the store can be delegated to a non-owner, 12:55, and the khazana are functionaries, not owners); (3) the wealth or content itself ('every thing has its khaza'in', 15:21, distinguishes container from contents); (4) hoarding or amassing (jm'/knz) - the reserve is meant to be released in measure (15:21) or spent (infaq, 17:100, opposed to amsaktum); (5) knowledge of the unseen (6:50, 11:31 list khaza'in and knowing the ghayb as two separate disclaimed claims); (6) origination/creation (15:21: stores pre-exist and are only sent down); (7) independent authority for the gate-custodians (40:49: Hell's khazana must themselves petition God).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 39:73:15:1 (khazanatuha of the Garden). These keepers hold no reserve, ration nothing in measure, and do not even interrogate for admission - they merely welcome ('salamun 'alaykum tibtum fadkhuluha'). The distinctive core (secured reserve dispensed by controlled measure) is fully bleached here, leaving only a bare attendant-at-the-gate. Even a 'guard against escape/confinement' reading fails, since these are ushers, not wardens. This anchors the khazana class as a resistant lexicalized custodial sub-class rather than a live realization of the reserve-sense.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Split into two synchronically distinct classes rather than one nucleus: (A/B) khaza'in/khazin = 'God's reserves dispensed in measure', internally welded (15:21-22) and self-glossed (12:55); and (C) khazana = 'the gate-wardens of the eschatological abodes', a fixed-referent personnel noun. The shared triliteral would then be etymological residue, since Class A's distinctive dispensation semantics is wholly absent from Class C and Class C's gate/interrogation semantics is wholly absent from A, and the only join ('custody') is thin enough to fit almost any guardianship root and is reached through morphology, which the contract disallows as semantic authority. This competitor is strong enough to forbid a STRONG grade, but is not adopted because 15:22 attests khazin as agent-of-keeping for a provision and khazana is the transparent agent-plural of that same khazin, so 'custodial keeping of a bounded thing' is genuinely common to both registers - the unified derivational family is the more parsimonious reading, and no analyst reached full UNRESOLVED.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently converge on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with a single custodial nucleus expressed as a derivational family. The narrow distinctive core (secured reserve held under exclusive/delegated custody, released only in controlled measure) is broad, self-glossing, and adversarially clean across the 8 khaza'in occurrences, and is welded to its agent face by the 15:21-22 pairing (khaza'inuhu with Us / you are not its khazinin). Covering the 4 khazana occurrences, however, forces a retreat to a thinner 'custody of a gated, access-controlled enclosure' abstraction: the sharp features (held-back reserve; release in measure) drop out entirely and are never Quran-internally attached to a khaza'in. Under the anti-over-grading rule, a coherent resistant lexicalized nominal sub-class caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE. The root is attested only nominally (no verbal forms), a further reason not to grade STRONG or claim UNIVERSAL/established. UNRESOLVED/multi-class is rejected because 15:22 supplies a clean morphological-and-semantic bridge from provision-keeper to place-keeper, so the classes are not fully unbridged. MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE/DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY is the disciplined call.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: khaza'in (broken plural fa'a'il): the secured reserve-repositories held under an owner's exclusive or delegated control, from which supply descends only in a controlled measure and which may be withheld. Distinctive features: enclosure/securedness, reserve/withholding, metered dispensation, exclusive proprietorship.
clusters.classification_rationale: Every occurrence sits in a possession/control frame (inda/inda-hum/inda-na, li-llah, tamlikun). 15:21 fixes the reserve+metered-release feature ('nothing exists but its khaza'in are with Us; We send it down only by a known measure'); 17:100 fixes the held-back/withholdable feature (khaza'in one could hold back, amsaktum, rather than spend, infaq); 12:55 grounds the sense concretely (grain-stores of Egypt) and separates xzn (the store) from hfz (the guarding-competence, hafiz). The recurring rhetorical move is denial that a human/opponent possesses these reserves (6:50, 11:31, 38:9, 52:37).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 15:21 'wa in min shay'in illa 'indana khaza'inuhu wa ma nunazziluhu illa bi-qadarin ma'lum'; 17:100 'law antum tamlikuna khaza'ina rahmati rabbi idhan la-amsaktum khashyata l-infaq'; 12:55 'ij'alni 'ala khaza'ini l-ardi inni hafizun 'alim'; 63:7 'wa li-llahi khaza'inu l-samawati wa l-ard'.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: khazin (active participle plural, agent face): the one who holds a provision in secured reserve/custody. Here negated of humans for the sky-water: 'you are not its keepers/storers'.
clusters.classification_rationale: Stands immediately after 15:21 (khaza'inuhu 'indana) and contrasts explicitly: the reserves are with Allah; humans are not the holders of that reserve. This is the internal keystone welding the place-face (Class A) to the agent-face - the same agent-of-keeping notion (khazin) that Class C pluralizes as khazana - and it applies to a concrete provision (water), not to gate-guarding.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 15:22 'fa-asqaynakumuhu wa ma antum lahu bi-khazinin' - agent-of-keeping of a provision, negated of humans, directly adjacent to 15:21's khaza'inuhu.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: khazana (agent-noun plural fa'ala): the angelic gate-custodians of the eschatological abodes, defined by threshold speech and gate-control, not by holding or dispensing a reserve. Reaches the root only through the thin 'custody of a bounded, access-controlled enclosure' feature; the distinctive reserve/metered-dispensation core is absent.
clusters.classification_rationale: In all four the khazana are stationed at opened gates (futihat abwabuha, 39:71/73) of Hell or the Garden and either interrogate arrivals (39:71, 67:8), receive petitions (40:49), or welcome (39:73). They store nothing and dispense nothing in measure; no verse attaches a khazana to a khaza'in. The link to the store-nucleus is available only via agent-noun morphology plus the weakest shared feature (custody of a gated holding), so this is a coherent resistant, quasi-lexicalized personnel sub-class rather than a live realization of the reserve-sense.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Bridged to the family by morphology (agent-plural of the khazin attested keeping a provision in 15:22) and by the shared enclosure/gate feature (abwabuha), so not declared fully unbridged; but the sharp reserve/metered-release features drop out, forcing the broadened 'custodial keeping of a bounded space' reading.
counterevidence: 39:73:15:1: the khazana of the Garden hold no reserve, ration nothing in measure, and do not interrogate - they merely welcome ('salamun 'alaykum tibtum fadkhuluha'), so the distinctive reserve/metered-dispensation core is fully bleached to a bare gate-attendant.

67:8:10:1: the khazana of Hell purely interrogate each incoming crowd ('alam ya'tikum nadhir'); nothing is stored, reserved, or released, so only the thin 'guard a bounded enclosure' reading reaches this occurrence.

39:71:14:1: the khazana of Hell interrogate the damned at the opened gates ('alam ya'tikum rusulun minkum'); the function is admission-control by challenge, not resource-storage or metered dispensation.
40:49:5:2: the damned petition the khazana of Hell to intercede with God ('ud'u rabbakum'), showing them to be powerless custodial intermediaries with zero storage or dispensation content.

reconciliation.rationale: Even the broadened 'guard a bounded enclosure' reading barely holds - these are ushers who merely welcome, with no reserve, no metered dispensation, and no admission-control. The distinctive core is fully bleached, so this is filed RESISTANT as the class's clearest resister rather than forced into the reserve-sense.

The khazana here are shown to be powerless (they must petition God to lighten punishment), so they administer no reserve and dispense nothing; the occurrence retains only threshold-custody and is filed with the resistant khazana sub-class.

adversarial_verification.notes: The distinctive reserve/metered-custody nucleus survives adversarial testing across Classes A and B (9/13, distinctiveness confirmed against hfz, knz, mlk via 12:55 and 17:100), so the core is not refuted. But Class C (khazana, 4/13) materially resists: the distinctive content is bleached to bare gate-custody. Because some occurrences resist while the core holds, the run is recorded as NOT_RUN (no clean PASSED with an empty failing set is available); the resisters are recorded rather than suppressed.

resistant_deep_analysis.preliminary_note: In all four the khazana are stationed at opened gates (futihat abwabuha, 39:71/73) of Hell or the Garden and either interrogate arrivals (39:71, 67:8), receive petitions (40:49), or welcome (39:73). They store nothing and dispense nothing in measure; no verse attaches a khazana to a khaza'in. The link to the store-nucleus is available only via agent-noun morphology plus the weakest shared feature (custody of a gated holding), so this is a coherent resistant, quasi-lexicalized personnel sub-class rather than a live realization of the reserve-sense.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each read all 13, each partitioned the data identically into khaza'in / khazin / khazana, and each independently graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with the khazana class as the resistant sub-class; the adversary's push toward a two-class split was tested and rejected only because of the 15:21-22 provision-keeper bridge.
candidate_root_contribution: xzn contributes the holding of something in secured custody within a bounded, access-controlled enclosure, realized in two morphological faces: the patient/place face khaza'in (the reserve-repository held under exclusive or delegated ownership, from which content is released only in a controlled measure and which may be withheld) and the agent face khazin/khazana (the one who keeps such a bounded holding and governs its boundary). The distinctive core (secured reserve + metered/controlled release) is broad and adversarially clean across the store-class and its provision-keeper agent, but attenuates to bare custody-of-a-gated-enclosure in the khazana sub-class.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 13 nominal occurrences, all QAC-tagged N: 8 khaza'in (6:50, 11:31, 12:55, 15:21, 17:100, 38:9, 52:37, 63:7), 1 khazinin (15:22), 4 khazana (39:71, 39:73, 40:49, 67:8). Decisive verbatim: 15:21 bi-qadarin ma'lum; 17:100 amsaktum/infaq; 12:55 hafiz over khaza'in; 39:71/73 futihat abwabuha.
layer_attribution.derivation: Three derivations of one triliteral: broken plural fa'a'il (khaza'in, place/patient face = the reserve-repository); active participle fa'il (khazin, agent face = provision-keeper); agent-noun plural fa'ala (khazana, agent face = gate-custodians). Morphology partitions patient-face from agent-face; it is used only as a partition signal, not as proof of cross-class semantic identity.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: khaza'in and khazin form the distinctive reserve/custody core; khazana is a coherent quasi-lexicalized personnel/warden sub-class (angelic gate-custodians of Hell/Garden) in which the distinctive reserve content is absent.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Contextual overlays - metered release (nunazzilu bi-qadar, 15:21), spend-vs-withhold (infaq/amsaktum, 17:100), gate-opening and threshold interrogation/greeting (39:71, 39:73, 67:8) - sharpen or attenuate the sense per occurrence but are NOT elevated into the root claim; the root contributes secured custody of a bounded holding, not the narrative acts around it.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary CONSISTENT filings of 39:73 and 40:49 under a broadened enclosure-custody reading were reconciled to RESISTANT because the distinctive reserve/metered-dispensation core is bleached; the khazana class is retained inside the derivational family via the 15:22 provision-keeper bridge but marked resistant rather than forced into the reserve-sense.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The khazana sub-class (39:71, 39:73, 40:49, 67:8) persists as material resistance: its distinctive meaning is gate-custody, never Quran-internally linked to a khaza'in, and reachable from the core only through the thin custody abstraction. This caps the judgment at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and is recorded, not suppressed.

hard_cases.reason: khazana of the Garden merely welcome; the distinctive reserve/metered-dispensation core is fully bleached, leaving a bare gate-attendant - the class's strongest resister.

evidence_basis.statement: 39:73:15:1: the khazana of the Garden hold no reserve, ration nothing in measure, and do not interrogate - they merely welcome ('salamun 'alaykum tibtum fadkhuluha'), so the distinctive reserve/metered-dispensation core is fully bleached to a bare gate-attendant.

hard_cases.reason: khazana purely interrogate arrivals at Hell's gate; nothing is stored, reserved, or released, so only the thin enclosure-custody reading reaches it.

evidence_basis.statement: 67:8:10:1: the khazana of Hell purely interrogate each incoming crowd ('alam ya'tikum nadhir'); nothing is stored, reserved, or released, so only the thin 'guard a bounded enclosure' reading reaches this occurrence.

hard_cases.reason: khazana interrogate the damned at opened gates; admission-control by challenge, not resource-storage or metered dispensation.

evidence_basis.statement: 39:71:14:1: the khazana of Hell interrogate the damned at the opened gates ('alam ya'tikum rusulun minkum'); the function is admission-control by challenge, not resource-storage or metered dispensation.

hard_cases.reason: khazana are powerless custodial intermediaries who must themselves petition God; no storage or dispensation content.

evidence_basis.statement: 40:49:5:2: the damned petition the khazana of Hell to intercede with God ('ud'u rabbakum'), showing them to be powerless custodial intermediaries with zero storage or dispensation content.

hard_case_representation.rationale: The core reserve/custody nucleus is PREFERRED and holds across Classes A and B, but the khazana sub-class (Class C, 4/13) materially resists the distinctive content and is carried as a coherent lexicalized resistant seam. Each resistant occurrence is represented by its own occurrence-text evidence basis, whose statement also appears as the strongest_counterexample (39:73) or in the Class C cluster counterevidence and occurrence overrides.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: The reserve/custody nucleus would be rejected if the khaza'in occurrences were shown Quran-internally to name the contents/wealth or the ownership relation itself (not the secured repository), OR if the khazana were shown to hold/measure a reserve - collapsing the claimed store-vs-keeper distinction and the reserve/metered-release feature.
rejection_condition.search_location: The khaza'in frames (15:21 'khaza'inuhu ... nunazziluhu bi-qadar'; 17:100 imsak/infaq; 12:55 hafiz-over-khaza'in; 63:7 li-llah) and every khazana occurrence (39:71, 39:73, 40:49, 67:8) checked for any attachment of khazana to a khaza'in or any storing/measuring act.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Re-read each occurrence's governing verbs and genitive frames; confirm whether xzn is predicated of a container/keeper vs of contents/ownership, and whether any khazana verse predicates holding/rationing rather than gate-speech.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Do not import 'reserve dispensed by measure' from adjacent lexemes (nunazzilu bi-qadar, infaq) into the root itself; separate xzn from hfz (12:55), knz, jm', and mlk; treat morphology as a partition signal only, not as proof of semantic identity across classes.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If khaza'in names contents/ownership or khazana are shown to store/measure, the derivational-family claim collapses; downgrade to UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY (two unbridged classes) or restate the nucleus at the thinner non-distinctive 'custody' altitude, revoking the REPRESENTATIVE reserve-sense.

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal reading is found that attaches a khazana to a khaza'in or shows the khazana holding/measuring/releasing a reserve (rather than opening gates, interrogating, welcoming, or relaying petitions in 39:71, 39:73, 40:49, 67:8), reopen to test promoting Class C from RESISTANT to CONSISTENT under a unified reserve-nucleus.

If the 15:21-22 adjacency bridge (khaza'inuhu 'indana / ma antum lahu bi-khazinin) is judged too weak to weld the place-face to the agent-face, reopen toward UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY with khaza'in/khazin and khazana as two unbridged partitions.
If 12:55's separation of khaza'in from hafiz is reanalyzed such that xzn absorbs the guarding-act (hfz) sense, reopen the semantic_boundary and the store-vs-guarding distinction.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The distinctive reserve/metered-custody nucleus survives adversarial testing across Classes A and B (9/13, distinctiveness confirmed against hfz, knz, mlk via 12:55 and 17:100), so the core is not refuted. But Class C (khazana, 4/13) materially resists: the distinctive content is bleached to bare gate-custody. Because some occurrences resist while the core holds, the run is recorded as NOT_RUN (no clean PASSED with an empty failing set is available); the resisters are recorded rather than suppressed.
